mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates elevated inflation, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and reduced equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship is consistently observed across the full range of CPIAUCSL values.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL is above its 12-month rolling average, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal activates when UNRATE crosses below 3.5%.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE is below 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The interaction effect is significant when both series show positive momentum.
evidence_refs: doc:BEA Retail Sales and Housing Data
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.05, or the positive return rate when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages is less than 55%.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO above 105.0), the economy is in a late-cycle expansion phase where corporate profits are strong but the risk of overheating increases, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. This mechanism is most potent in the late-cycle regime.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO exceeds 105.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 3.5% signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across the full range of RSAFS values.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS is above its 12-month rolling average, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals an economic slowdown that reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal activates when INDPRO falls below 100.0.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO is below 100.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (measured by RSAFS) indicates a strong demand environment that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The interaction effect is significant when both series show positive momentum relative to their 3-month averages.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.05, or the positive return rate when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages is less than 55%.
